q6.answer: Status is stored in the status column of a new report_exports row on the primary database (queued, running, done, failed). The page learns of changes by polling GET /api/reports/{report_id}/export every 5 seconds while queued or running, and on reopening it reads the user's newest export row (highest created_at), so the stored state is always what it gets.

q7.answer: It streams. The job pages through iter_report_rows (2,000 rows per keyset query, replica only), formats each page into an in-memory buffer, and uploads it as a multipart part whenever the buffer reaches 8 MB. It holds only one buffer, one page and the etag list (about 113 etags), never the whole report, so memory stays far below 512 MB.

q8.answer: The data is never visible, because nothing appears at the object key until complete_multipart succeeds. On an exception the job aborts the multipart upload and re-raises. If the worker dies or times out, the bucket's 24-hour rule discards the orphaned parts. The next attempt starts again from the beginning with a fresh upload to the same key, because the queue keeps no progress and the plan keeps none.

q9.answer: They are copied from the page URL into the click request and stored as the filters and cols snapshot columns on the report_exports row, inserted at click time. The job payload carries only the export_id, and the job loads the row to get filters and cols. The user_id comes from the session, not the browser.

q10.answer: A partial unique index on (user_id, report_id) WHERE status IN ('queued','running') in the primary database. When two inserts race, one succeeds and the other is rejected. The rejected request selects the existing row and returns it, so there is one row and one job.

q11.answer: Before the email is sent, complete_multipart must have succeeded so the whole file exists, and the row must be marked done. The job then makes the signed URL and sends the email, then sets notified_at. If the queue runs the job again, it loads the row: done with notified_at set returns without rebuilding or emailing. Done with notified_at null skips the rebuild and only sends the email. A failed row returns. If the done update changes zero rows, it reloads and follows the same rules.

q12.answer: Nothing is stored and there is no retry. If it fails before streaming starts, the API returns an error status. If it fails after streaming has begun, the status is already sent, so the connection is cut mid-body. There is no Content-Length and the transfer is chunked, so the browser treats it as a failed download, and the error is logged. The user can click again.
